entities.name: RAG1
observations: The 768-aa sequence is identified by high-similarity curated vertebrate homologs as V(D)J recombination-activating protein 1 (RAG1).
Sequence contains Pfam RAG1_imp_bd at residues 13–310, C3HC4 zinc finger at 312–350, RAG1 and DNA-binding domains at 418–548, and pre-RNase H/RNase H-like domains at 549–757.
Curated homolog annotations describe RAG1 as the catalytic component of the RAG complex, with DNA endonuclease and E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase activities.
RAG1-mediated DNA cleavage requires RAG2 in the RAG complex and Mg2+ or Mn2+ as divalent metal cofactor.
Sequence-derived properties: 768 aa, approximately 85.8 kDa, theoretical pI 8.72.

entities.name: RAG1 DNA cleavage
observations: RAG1 first nicks one DNA strand adjacent to a recombination signal sequence; the resulting 3'-OH attacks the opposite phosphodiester bond by transesterification, generating coding-end hairpins and blunt signal ends.
The reaction is a metal-dependent DNA endonuclease activity performed in the RAG1-RAG2 complex.

entities.name: RAG1 ubiquitin transfer
observations: RAG1 is annotated as an E3 ubiquitin-protein ligase that promotes transfer of ubiquitin from an E2 active-site cysteine to a lysine on an acceptor protein, including monoubiquitination of histone H3 in the V(D)J recombination context.

entities.name: V(D)J recombination
observations: RAG1 functions in the RAG complex to initiate immunoglobulin and T-cell receptor gene rearrangement in developing lymphocytes.

entities.name: RAG2
observations: RAG2 is a required noncatalytic partner of RAG1 for known RAG-mediated DNA cleavage activities.
